Summary:
Mapped `/workspace/NepalCasts/NepalCasts` as a multi-tier web app: Vite/React SPA frontend with Clerk auth and Firebase client SDK, an Express 5 API under `server/src`, Firebase callable/scheduled functions under `functions/src`, and Vercel serverless shims under `api/`. Identified frontend/public/protected/admin routes, Express route groups, callable function surface, auth/authz design, main Firestore collections/subcollections, Cloudinary/OneSignal/FCM integrations, and several high-risk drift areas for follow-on validation. No exploit testing was performed. Shared detailed notes via note IDs `25efca` (architecture map) and `29c97a` (methodology).

Findings:
- Framework/runtime: React 18 + Vite SPA (`src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`), React Router v7, Clerk frontend auth, Firebase client services, Express backend (`server/src/index.ts`), Firebase Functions (`functions/src/index.ts`), Vercel rewrites/serverless shims (`vercel.json`, `api/*.js`).
- Frontend auth flow: Clerk session is mirrored into Firebase via custom token sign-in in `src/providers/AppProviders.tsx`; app syncs `users/{uid}` and `profiles/{uid}` records and computes `isAdmin` from Firestore plus a hardcoded super-admin email path.
- Backend auth/authz: Express verifies Firebase ID tokens in `server/src/middleware/auth.ts`; admin access generally relies on `req.user?.admin === true`, while some serverless shims also fall back to `users/{uid}.isAdmin` and may auto-set custom claims (`api/admin-users.js`).
- Primary route/view surface: public discovery/profile/casting/auth pages, protected `/messages`, `/settings`, `/notifications`, `/saved`, `/calls`, `/applications`, and `/admin/*` feature areas under `src/routes/*.tsx`.
- Primary API surface: profile, casting, messaging, uploads, notifications, admin routes under `server/src/routes/*`, plus callable Functions for profile, messaging, casting, notifications, admin moderation/data-request actions in `functions/src/handlers/*`.
- Data stores/integrations: Firestore is dominant (`users`, `profiles`, `casting_calls`, `conversations/messages`, `notifications`, `calls`, `reports`, `admin_logs`, `data_requests`, `users/{uid}/private/settings`, `users/{uid}/media`); Realtime DB is initialized client-side; Cloudinary handles media; OneSignal and FCM handle push; background Firestore listeners generate notifications/call alerts/casting alerts.
- Security-relevant drift: active `firestore.rules` and `storage.rules` are globally permissive (`allow read, write: if true`) despite README claims and `server/src/tests/firestoreRules.test.ts` expecting restrictive rules; multiple admin/content frontend components still perform direct Firestore writes, especially under `src/features/admin/*`.
- Notable high-risk components for validation: direct Firestore-admin surfaces, mixed enforcement between client/Express/Functions, upload/media ownership paths (`server/src/routes/upload.routes.ts`), proxy/shim layer (`api/proxy.js`, `api/admin-users.js`), messaging/profile/casting object ownership logic, and private notification token storage under `users/{uid}/private/settings`.

Recommendations:
- Prioritize a dedicated Firestore/Storage authorization validation agent to test whether permissive rules enable cross-user read/write of `users`, `profiles`, `reports`, `admin_logs`, `private` docs, and media metadata.
- Spawn an admin-surface validation agent focused on `src/features/admin/*`, `server/src/routes/admin.routes.ts`, `functions/src/handlers/admin.ts`, and `api/admin-users.js` to check privilege escalation and enforcement consistency.
- Spawn a BOLA/IDOR agent for messaging/profile/casting paths across both direct Firestore access and backend APIs/functions.
- Spawn an upload/integration agent for `server/src/routes/upload.routes.ts`, `server/src/middleware/uploadSecurity.ts`, `server/src/config/cloudinary.ts`, and `api/proxy.js` to assess ownership checks, unsigned upload fallback, and proxy trust boundaries.
